title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integrations, Escalations, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Lina Patel
body:
Purpose and scope:

This playbook describes the standard process and checklists Customer Success (CS) and Support use for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference. It consolidates integration requirements, the escalation playbook, known issues and workarounds, the support process, ongoing health-check cadence, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) materials. Audience: CS, Support, Solutions Engineering, and Customer Platform/Infra teams.

1) Quick intro and success criteria

- Goal: get enterprise customers to production with predictable latency, cost, and observability within 6–8 weeks.
- Success criteria (must be met before graduation):
  - Production traffic served with SLA-compliant latency (p50 < 200ms, p95 < 800ms) for the agreed workload profile.
  - Integration tests pass (auth, networking, model selection, rate limiting).
  - Observability and billing visibility configured in Console.
  - Runbook & escalation contacts documented and validated.

2) Onboarding phases (high-level)

Phase A — Discovery (week 0–1)
1. Kickoff with customer stakeholders (CS, engineering, security). Capture success criteria, compliance needs, and throughput/latency targets.
2. Assign primary owner (CS AE) and technical owner (Solutions Engineer).
3. Share onboarding plan and timeline in shared Confluence page.

Phase B — Integration & Test (week 1–4)
1. Networking & Auth: validate VPC/VPN setup for Private deployments or IP allowlist for hosted.
2. Model and prompts: confirm model version and evaluation prompts.
3. Performance baseline: run smoke tests to capture baseline token/sec and latency.
4. Observability: configure dashboards, tracing, and cost tagging.
5. Conduct integration checklist (table below).

Phase C — Pilot & Tuning (week 4–6)
1. Pilot with staged traffic and synthetic load.
2. Tune batching, max_tokens, and caching settings.
3. Validate fallback/rollout policies.
4. Finalize SLOs, runbooks, and escalation contacts.

Phase D — Production Rollout (week 6–8)
1. Canary rollout to 5–10% traffic, monitor for errors/regressions for 72 hours.
2. Gradual ramp every 24–48 hours with post-ramp checks.
3. Transition to quarterly health checks and QBR cadence.

3) Integration checklist (must be completed during Phase B)

- Preconditions table:

| Item | Owner | Acceptance Criteria | Example/Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Account & billing setup | CS | Billing active, quota assigned | Confirm billing contact in Console |
| Auth/Keys | Customer | API keys exchanged or SAML configured | For Private, KMS/HSM integration validated |
| Network connectivity | Customer/Infra | VPN/VPC peering or IP allowlist confirmed | Include CIDR and firewall rules |
| Model selection | Customer/SE | Model version pinned for pilot | Document quantization profile if used |
| Observability | SE/CS | Dashboards & traces enabled | Provide dashboard links and alert rules |
| Rate limits & quotas | CS/Support | Quota set and tested | Include burst policy if required |

- Common commands and examples:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"rwd-small-v1","input":"Hello"}'

terraform snippet for allowed IPs (example):
```
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "allow_redwood" {
  type        = "ingress"
  from_port   = 443
  to_port     = 443
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = ["203.0.113.0/24"]
}
```

4) Escalation playbook (operational steps)

Severity definitions:
- Sev1 (Critical): Production outage affecting >= 50% of customers' requests, or system-wide failure.
- Sev2 (High): Degraded service impacting a subset of requests or customers, significant performance regression.
- Sev3 (Medium): Functional bug with workaround; no immediate business impact.
- Sev4 (Low): Cosmetic or documentation issue.

Escalation steps (1–2 hour action windows for Sev1/Sev2):
1. Triage (Support oncall): gather logs, request ids, region, model, and exact client payloads.
2. Notify CS and SE: open dedicated Slack channel #inc-sevX-[customer]-[shortid] and invite owners.
3. Immediate mitigations: apply routing fallbacks (model variant), increase replica count, or disable problematic feature flags.
4. Engage SRE and Runtime oncall for kernel/scheduling or capacity issues.
5. If customer-impacting, schedule executive comms (CS manager + Account Executive) within 2 hours.
6. Post-incident: own a 72-hour stabilization plan and schedule a postmortem within 7 calendar days.

Escalation matrix (contact order):

| Role | Primary contact | Escalate to |
|---|---|---|
| Support oncall | support-oncall@redwood.ai | SRE oncall |
| Solutions Engineer | se-team@redwood.ai | Eng runtime lead |
| Customer Success | cs-ae@redwood.ai | CS manager |
| SRE/Infra | sre-oncall@redwood.ai | Infrastructure manager |

5) Known issues and workarounds (maintain short, actionable entries)

- Known issue: Long tail p99 latency regressions on rwd-large-v2 under mixed-batch workloads.
  - Symptoms: p95 stable, p99 spikes > 2x normal during bursty traffic.
  - Workaround: switch to pinned single-model replicas with batching disabled for affected routes; set request_max_batch_wait_ms=0.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

- Known issue: Token accounting mismatch for multi-part streaming responses in older SDK versions (<1.4.0).
  - Symptoms: billing mismatch reported by customer.
  - Workaround: upgrade SDK to 1.4.0+ or use response_metadata to reconcile tokens.
  - Owner: eng-developer-experience.

- Known issue: Private deployment onboarding failing when HSM certs are rotated mid-setup.
  - Symptoms: connector reports TLS handshake errors.
  - Workaround: follow cert-rotation ordering in onprem-packaging doc: import CA -> rotate node certs -> restart routing service.
  - Owner: eng-private-deployments.

6) Support process and SLAs

- Tickets: All inbound enterprise tickets go into Zendesk with "enterprise" tag and are triaged within 1 hour during business hours.
- SLAs:
  - Initial response: Sev1 15 minutes, Sev2 1 hour, Sev3 4 hours, Sev4 2 business days.
  - Time-to-resolution target: Sev1 < 6 hours (workaround) and full remediation in < 72 hours.
- Communication: CS owns customer-facing updates; Support owns technical diagnostics. Use shared Slack channel for real-time updates and keep Zendesk ticket updated with timeline and next steps.

7) Health checks, monitoring, and QBRs

- Weekly health check items (automated + manual):
  - Traffic volume and token usage trend vs budget.
  - Error rate (5xx) by route and model — target <0.05% sustained.
  - Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 tracked and annotated.
  - Cost-per-1k tokens and any anomalies.
  - Open action items from previous week.

- Monthly operational review: SE + CS + customer infra to review incidents, performance tuning, and capacity forecasts.

- Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template (use for customer-facing slides):
  - Executive summary: uptime, consumption, major incidents, value realized.
  - Metrics snapshot: tokens, latencies, cost trends, ROI indicators.
  - Roadmap & upcoming deprecations: highlight model/feature changes that affect production.
  - Action items and owners (clearly assigned).

8) Runbooks & playbooks referenced

- Link: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture — runtime troubleshooting.
- Link: confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity — capacity planning for Dedicated.
- Link: confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides — private deployment steps.

9) Ownership and handoffs

- Primary owner: Customer Success (onboarding AE).
- Technical owner: Solutions Engineering.
- Long-term support: Support + SRE for operational incidents.
- Escalation owners must be listed in the customer onboarding checklist and validated by last_updated date.

10) Templates and artifacts to attach (checklist)

- Onboarding plan (shared Confluence page).
- Integration test suite results (zip or link).
- Pilot performance report (CSV with latency quantiles).
- Runbook for the customer with escalation contacts and routing policies.
- QBR slide deck template (customer-facing).

Appendix: Troubleshooting quick commands

- Fetch request logs by request id (example):
  - kubectl logs -l app=request-processor -c processor | grep <REQUEST_ID>
- Trigger cache flush for a customer prefix (SE tool):
  - se-tools flush-prefix --customer-id=<CID> --prefix=<PROMPT_PREFIX>
- Increase replica count for model pool (SRE API):
  - POST /internal/pools/<pool-id>/scale {"replicas": 10} (internal only)

If anything in this playbook conflicts with a customer's contractual terms, contact Legal & Finance before proceeding. For playbook feedback or updates, add suggestions to the page comments and tag the document owner.
